title: Performance Metrics Calculator
description: Three live conversions from a raw cycle count to execution time, throughput, and speedup factor, each showing its formula and substituted operands.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Benchmarking
Performance Analysis

educational.topic: Converting cycle counts to reportable metrics
learningObjectives: Compute execution time from cycles and clock frequency
prerequisites: A cycle counter yields elapsed cycles

controls.label: Load Chapter 12 example
controls.purpose: Reproduce the 140 ms FFT versus 20.5 s DFT comparison

assumptions: Clock frequency is constant during the measurement
The comparison baseline measured the same work
limitations: Assumes one operation per measured interval; batched measurements need division by the batch size first

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Live calculator with formulas and substituted operands shown
keyQuestions: Which metrics change when only the clock changes?
What must accompany a speedup factor for it to be reproducible?
commonMisconceptions: That a speedup factor alone is a complete result
That raising the clock improves the algorithm
assessmentOpportunities: Identify what cannot be determined from a bare speedup claim
